questions.title: Acyclovir is used to inhibit herpes viruses
questions.question: Which ONE of the following drugs is used to inhibit herpes viruses?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Azidothymidine (zidovudine) is an anti-HIV nucleoside reverse-transcriptase inhibitor, not a herpesvirus drug.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Oseltamivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor used against influenza, not herpesviruses.
explanations.C: Correct. Acyclovir is a guanosine nucleoside analogue used to inhibit herpesviruses (herpes simplex and varicella-zoster). It is selectively activated by the viral thymidine kinase and then incorporated by the viral DNA polymerase to terminate the growing viral DNA chain, giving selectivity for infected cells.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Amantadine is an M2 ion-channel blocker used against influenza A, not herpesviruses.

questions.title: Valacyclovir is the oral drug for genital herpes after topical therapy
questions.question: A 27-year-old nursing mother is diagnosed as suffering from genital herpes. She has a history of this viral infection and previously responded to a drug used topically. Apart from her current problem she is in good health. Which drug to be used orally is most likely to be prescribed at this time?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Foscarnet is reserved for acyclovir-resistant HSV or ganciclovir-resistant CMV and is given intravenously with significant toxicity, not as a first oral choice here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Ritonavir is an anti-HIV protease inhibitor, not a herpes simplex drug.
explanations.C: Correct. Valacyclovir is the L-valyl ester prodrug of acyclovir, giving much better oral bioavailability. It is therefore the oral drug most likely to be prescribed for genital herpes in a patient previously controlled with a topical agent. Foscarnet, ritonavir and amantadine are not appropriate oral herpes simplex agents in this setting.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Amantadine is an anti-influenza agent, not a herpes simplex drug.

questions.title: Ganciclovir suppresses herpetic infection and provides CMV retinitis prophylaxis
questions.question: The drug most likely to suppress herpetic infections and provide prophylaxis against CMV retinitis in this patient is

explanations.A: Incorrect. Indinavir is an anti-HIV protease inhibitor, with no activity against herpesviruses or CMV.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Fluconazole is an antifungal, not an antiviral.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Rifabutin is used for mycobacterial (MAC) prophylaxis, not for herpesvirus or CMV suppression.
explanations.D: Correct. Ganciclovir is a guanosine analogue whose activity extends beyond herpes simplex to cytomegalovirus. It can therefore both suppress herpetic infection and provide prophylaxis against CMV retinitis in an immunocompromised patient. Indinavir, fluconazole and rifabutin have no useful activity against herpesviruses or CMV.

questions.title: Vidarabine is not effective in eradication of HCV
questions.question: All the following agents can be used effectively in eradication of HCV EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS effective). Sofosbuvir is a direct-acting NS5B polymerase inhibitor and a mainstay of hepatitis C eradication.
explanations.B: Correct. Vidarabine is an old herpesvirus agent and is NOT effective against hepatitis C virus. It is therefore the exception among these options. Sofosbuvir, interferon-alpha and ribavirin are all established components of HCV eradication.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS effective). Interferon-alpha has an established role in hepatitis C therapy, classically combined with ribavirin.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS effective). Ribavirin is used in combination regimens to eradicate HCV.

questions.title: Lamivudine is not effective in eradication of influenza virus
questions.question: All the following agents can be used effectively in eradication of influenza virus EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS effective). Amantadine is an M2 ion-channel blocker active against influenza A.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it IS effective). Oseltamivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor active against influenza.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS effective). Rimantadine, like amantadine, is an M2 blocker used against influenza A.
explanations.D: Correct. Lamivudine is a hepatitis-B/HIV nucleoside reverse-transcriptase inhibitor and is NOT an influenza drug. It is therefore the exception among these options. Amantadine, oseltamivir and rimantadine are all genuinely active against influenza.

questions.title: Oseltamivir eradicates H1N1 influenza by inhibiting viral neuraminidase
questions.question: Oseltamivir can eradicate H1N1 influenza virus through:

options.D: Inhibition of the viral neuraminidase enzyme

explanations.A: Incorrect. Oseltamivir does not act on viral RNA replication.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Influenza is an RNA virus and oseltamivir does not target DNA replication.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Inhibition of viral uncoating is the mechanism of the M2 blockers amantadine and rimantadine, not oseltamivir.
explanations.D: Correct. Oseltamivir inhibits the viral neuraminidase enzyme. As a result, newly assembled H1N1 virions cannot be cleaved free from the host-cell surface, halting viral release and spread. It does not act on viral RNA/DNA replication or on uncoating, which is the M2-blocker mechanism.

questions.title: Interferons are not used for remission of CMV retinitis
questions.question: Interferons are protective glycoproteins that can be used effectively in management of all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.A: Genital warts induced through refractory condylomata acuminata infection
options.C: Combined with ribavirin to improve the rate of remission of Hepatitis C virus infection

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS an indication). Interferon is used for refractory condylomata acuminata (genital warts).
explanations.B: Correct. Interferons are NOT used for remission of CMV retinitis, which is treated with ganciclovir. This is therefore the exception among interferon indications. Condylomata acuminata, chronic HBV and HCV (with ribavirin) are, by contrast, genuine interferon indications.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS an indication). Interferon combined with ribavirin improves remission of hepatitis C.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS an indication). Interferon is used in chronic hepatitis B infection.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: An ulcerated mass with atypical cells is best described as a carcinoma
questions.question: A 62-year-old male patient has hematuria many times in the past week. Cytological examination of the urine shows atypical cells. Cystoscopy shows a 5 cm ulcerated mass. Which of the following best describes the lesion?

explanations.A: Correct. An ulcerated mass with atypical (malignant) cells arising from epithelium is a carcinoma, the malignant tumour of epithelial origin. The bladder urothelium is epithelial, so its malignancy is a carcinoma. Sarcoma is mesenchymal, while adenoma and papilloma are benign epithelial tumours.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Sarcoma is a malignant tumour of mesenchymal (connective-tissue) origin, not epithelial.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adenoma is a benign tumour of glandular epithelium and would not present as an ulcerated mass with atypical cells.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Papilloma is a benign tumour of surface epithelium, not a malignant ulcerated lesion.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Adenocarcinoma is a malignant tumour of glands
questions.question: Adenocarcinoma is a:

explanations.A: Correct. Adenocarcinoma is the malignant tumour of glandular epithelium. The prefix 'adeno-' marks the glandular origin and the '-carcinoma' marks the malignant epithelial nature. By contrast, a benign glandular tumour is an adenoma and a benign surface-epithelial tumour is a papilloma.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A hamartoma is a mass of disorganised but mature indigenous tissue, not a glandular malignancy.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A benign tumour of glands is an adenoma, not an adenocarcinoma.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A benign tumour of surface epithelium is a papilloma.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: A grade I, stage I neoplasm is well-differentiated and localized
questions.question: Review of surgical pathology reports indicates that a certain neoplasm is diagnosed as grade I on a scale of I to IV. Clinically, some patients with this neoplasm are found to have stage I disease. Which of the following is the best interpretation of a neoplasm with these designations?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Grade and stage describe differentiation and spread of an established malignancy; a low grade does not mean the lesion is not malignant.
explanations.B: Correct. Grade reports microscopic differentiation, so grade I means well-differentiated. Stage reports the anatomical extent of spread, so stage I means localized. A grade I, stage I neoplasm is therefore both well-differentiated and localized.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Origin from epithelium is not what grade and stage designate; they describe differentiation and spread.
explanations.D: Incorrect. An in situ component is not implied by a grade I, stage I designation.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Signet ring carcinoma is a type of glandular carcinoma
questions.question: Signet ring carcinoma is a type of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Squamous cell carcinoma arises from squamous epithelium and does not show the mucin-filled signet-ring cell.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Transitional cell carcinoma arises from urothelium, not glandular epithelium.
explanations.C: Correct. Signet ring carcinoma is a glandular (adeno)carcinoma in which intracytoplasmic mucin displaces the nucleus to the cell periphery. This mucin-secreting behaviour is the hallmark of a glandular origin, classically in the stomach. It is therefore a form of adenocarcinoma, not a squamous, transitional or basal cell carcinoma.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Basal cell carcinoma is a skin tumour of basal keratinocytes, unrelated to the signet-ring glandular type.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: The edges of a malignant ulcer are everted
questions.question: The edges of the malignant ulcer are:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Inverted edges are not the feature of a malignant ulcer.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Undermined edges are characteristic of a tuberculous ulcer, not a malignant one.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Sharp, punched-out edges are characteristic of a syphilitic (gummatous) ulcer.
explanations.D: Correct. A malignant ulcer characteristically has raised and everted edges. The everted margin reflects proliferating tumour tissue heaping up over the ulcer edge, and the base is typically indurated. Inverted, undermined and sharp edges point instead to other ulcer types.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Stroma separating individual cells differentiates sarcoma from carcinoma
questions.question: The most important histologic feature that differentiates sarcoma from carcinoma is:

options.D: Criteria of malignancy are more prominent

explanations.A: Incorrect. Necrosis can occur in both sarcomas and carcinomas and is not the distinguishing feature.
explanations.B: Correct. In a sarcoma the malignant cells are diffuse, with stroma (reticulin) running between individual cells. In a carcinoma the cells are cohesive in nests, with stroma around the groups rather than around each cell. This stromal relationship is the key differentiating histologic feature between the two.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Vascularity is not the defining discriminator between the two.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Criteria of malignancy (atypia, mitoses) appear in both and do not by themselves separate sarcoma from carcinoma.

questions.learning_objective: State that the stromal relationship (stroma separating individual cells) distinguishes sarcoma from carcinoma.

questions.title: Bleomycin (iron/oxygen DNA strand breaks, pulmonary toxicity) acts in G2 phase
questions.question: A drug used in a chemotherapy regimen works by complexing with iron and oxygen to promote DNA strand breaks. While on this drug the patient must be monitored closely due to pulmonary side effects. In what phase of the cell cycle does this drug work?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Bleomycin does not act principally in G1.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The M phase is where the vinca alkaloids and taxanes act, not bleomycin.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The S phase is where antimetabolites act; bleomycin is not S-phase specific.
explanations.D: Correct. The drug described complexes iron and oxygen to break DNA and carries pulmonary toxicity, which identifies it as bleomycin. Bleomycin acts principally in the G2 phase of the cell cycle. Its risk of pulmonary fibrosis is the reason lung function must be monitored.

questions.title: The cellular target of paclitaxel is microtubules
questions.question: The cellular target of paclitaxel is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Paclitaxel does not target deoxyribonucleotides.
explanations.B: Correct. Paclitaxel binds beta-tubulin and hyper-stabilises microtubules. Because the spindle microtubules can no longer disassemble, the cell arrests in mitosis. Its cellular target is therefore the microtubule, not DNA, topoisomerase or a tyrosine kinase.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Topoisomerase is the target of drugs such as irinotecan and etoposide, not paclitaxel.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Tyrosine kinase is the target of drugs such as imatinib, not paclitaxel.

questions.title: Cisplatin causes nephrotoxicity rather than bone marrow suppression
questions.question: Which of the following medications has the major side effect of nephrotoxicity rather than bone marrow suppression?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Methotrexate's dose-limiting toxicities include myelosuppression and mucositis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Doxorubicin is characteristically cardiotoxic and also myelosuppressive.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Vinblastine is markedly myelosuppressive.
explanations.D: Correct. Cisplatin's major dose-limiting toxicity is nephrotoxicity rather than bone-marrow suppression. It is managed with vigorous hydration to protect the kidneys. Methotrexate, doxorubicin and vinblastine, by contrast, are characteristically myelosuppressive.

questions.title: Methotrexate is the folic acid analog anticancer drug
questions.question: Which of the following anticancer drugs is a folic acid analog?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Fluorouracil is a pyrimidine analog, not a folic-acid analog.
explanations.B: Correct. Methotrexate is a folic-acid analog that competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase. Blocking this enzyme depletes the reduced folate needed for thymidylate and purine synthesis. Fluorouracil is a pyrimidine analog, while irinotecan and cyclophosphamide act by other mechanisms.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Irinotecan is a topoisomerase I inhibitor.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating agent, not an antifolate.

questions.learning_objective: Identify methotrexate as the anticancer drug that is a folic acid analog.

questions.title: Cyclophosphamide is a cell-cycle non-specific agent
questions.question: Which of the following anticancer drugs is a cell cycle non-specific agent?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Vinblastine is a vinca alkaloid acting in the M phase, so it is cell-cycle specific.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Methotrexate is an S-phase antimetabolite, so it is cell-cycle specific.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Vincristine is a vinca alkaloid acting in the M phase, so it is cell-cycle specific.
explanations.D: Correct. Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating agent that damages DNA in any phase of the cell cycle. This makes it the classic cell-cycle non-specific agent, active even against slowly dividing cells. Vinblastine, methotrexate and vincristine, by contrast, are cell-cycle specific.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: A congenital, stable reddish cutaneous nodule is a haemangioma
questions.question: A 14-year-old healthy girl has a 0.3 cm reddish, slightly raised nodule on the skin of the upper chest found on routine examination. It has been present since birth and has not appreciably changed in size or colour. Which of the following neoplasms is this nodule most likely to be?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Melanoma is a malignant pigmented tumour that changes over time, unlike this lifelong stable nodule.
explanations.B: Correct. A small, reddish, slightly raised nodule present since birth and unchanged is characteristically a haemangioma. A haemangioma is a benign tumour of blood vessels, which explains its red colour. Melanoma, carcinoma and lymphoma would not be congenital and stable in this way.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Carcinoma is a malignancy of adults that would not be congenital and unchanging.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Lymphoma presents as lymphoid masses, not a stable congenital skin nodule.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: A soft, painless, stable subcutaneous mass is a lipoma
questions.question: A 27-year-old woman in excellent health has a 2 cm soft, rounded mass palpable beneath the skin of the left forearm. There is no difficulty using the arm and no pain on movement or palpation. The overlying skin is normal, and the mass does not change in size over the next year. Which of the following neoplasms is she most likely to have?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Rhabdomyosarcoma is a malignant, rapidly growing tumour, unlike this soft, painless, size-stable mass.
explanations.B: Correct. A soft, rounded, painless, mobile subcutaneous mass that does not change in size is characteristically a lipoma. A lipoma is a benign tumour of adipose tissue, which accounts for its soft consistency. Rhabdomyosarcoma, melanoma and metastatic carcinoma would be firmer or progressive.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Melanoma is a pigmented skin malignancy, not a soft subcutaneous fatty mass.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Metastatic carcinoma would typically be firm and progressive, not a soft stable nodule in a healthy young woman.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: An ovarian cystic mass with hair and multiple tissues is a teratoma
questions.question: A 32-year-old woman has dull pelvic pain for two months. An 8 cm mass involving the right ovary is excised. On gross inspection the surface is smooth and not adherent; on sectioning it is cystic and filled with hair. Microscopically there is squamous epithelium, tall columnar glandular epithelium, cartilage, and fibrous connective tissue. Which of the following neoplasms is she most likely to have?

explanations.A: Incorrect. A choristoma is normal tissue at an ectopic site, not a cystic mass containing multiple mature tissues from all germ layers.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A myxoma is a benign tumour of primitive myxoid connective tissue, not a multi-tissue cystic mass.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A hamartoma is a disorganised mass of tissue indigenous to the site, not a tumour containing hair, cartilage and glandular epithelium together.
explanations.D: Correct. A cystic ovarian mass containing hair, squamous and glandular epithelium, cartilage and fibrous tissue is a teratoma. A teratoma is derived from all three germ cell layers, which is why it contains such varied tissues (a mature dermoid cyst). Choristoma, myxoma and hamartoma do not combine tissues from all three germ layers.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: A solid, circumscribed, slow-growing uterine nodule is a leiomyoma
questions.question: A 35-year-old woman had a firm nodule palpable on the dome of the uterus six years ago. The nodule has slowly increased in size and is now about twice its original size. By ultrasound it is solid and circumscribed. She remains asymptomatic. Which of the following neoplasms is she most likely to have?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Leiomyosarcoma is a malignant smooth-muscle tumour that grows rapidly and is often symptomatic, unlike this slow, circumscribed, asymptomatic nodule.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Haemangioma is a vascular tumour, not the typical solid circumscribed uterine nodule.
explanations.C: Correct. A firm, solid, circumscribed uterine nodule that enlarges slowly while the patient stays asymptomatic is characteristically a leiomyoma (fibroid). It is the benign tumour of uterine smooth muscle. Its malignant counterpart, leiomyosarcoma, grows rapidly and is often symptomatic.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Adenocarcinoma is a malignant glandular tumour and would not present as a slow-growing, circumscribed, asymptomatic uterine nodule.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: The benign tumour of cartilage is a chondroma
questions.question: Benign tumor of cartilage is called a/an:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Lipoma is the benign tumour of adipose tissue.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Leiomyoma is the benign tumour of smooth muscle.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Osteoma is the benign tumour of bone.
explanations.D: Correct. Chondroma is the benign tumour of cartilage. Its name follows the rule of tissue-of-origin plus the '-oma' suffix for a benign tumour. Lipoma, leiomyoma and osteoma are the benign tumours of fat, smooth muscle and bone respectively.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: A hamartoma is a mass of disorganised but mature indigenous cells
questions.question: Hamartoma refers to:

options.A: Mass of disorganised but mature cells indigenous to the part
options.C: Tumour differentiating towards more than one cell line
options.D: Mass of ectopic rests of normal tissue

explanations.A: Correct. A hamartoma is a mass of disorganised but mature cells indigenous to the part in which it arises. It is an excess of normally-present tissue arranged haphazardly. This distinguishes it from a teratoma (totipotent cells) and a choristoma (ectopic normal tissue).
explanations.B: Incorrect. A tumour arising from totipotent cells describes a teratoma.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Differentiation towards more than one cell line describes a mixed/teratomatous tumour, not a hamartoma.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A mass of ectopic rests of normal tissue describes a choristoma, not a hamartoma.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Malignant tumours arising from glandular cells are called adenocarcinoma
questions.question: Malignant tumours are:

options.A: When arising from glandular cells are called adenocarcinoma
options.D: When arising from epithelial cells are called sarcomas

explanations.A: Correct. A malignant tumour arising from glandular cells is called an adenocarcinoma. Malignant tumours are typically poorly differentiated and readily metastasise. A malignancy of epithelial cells is a carcinoma, not a sarcoma, which arises from mesenchyme.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Malignant tumours are typically poorly differentiated, not well differentiated.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Malignant tumours characteristically metastasise; that capacity defines malignancy.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Malignant tumours arising from epithelial cells are carcinomas; sarcomas arise from mesenchymal tissue.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Neuroblastoma is an embryonic tumour
questions.question: Neuroblastoma is a/an:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Neuroblastoma is not of epithelial origin.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Neuroblastoma is not a mesenchymal (connective-tissue) tumour.
explanations.C: Correct. Neuroblastoma is an embryonic (blastoma) tumour. It arises from immature neural crest precursor cells. It is therefore neither an epithelial, mesenchymal nor germ-cell tumour.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Neuroblastoma is not a germ-cell tumour.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Seminoma is not an embryonic tumour
questions.question: The following tumour is NOT an embryonic tumour:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS embryonic). Retinoblastoma is an embryonic tumour of the retina.
explanations.B: Incorrect (it IS embryonic). Medulloblastoma is an embryonic tumour of the cerebellum.
explanations.C: Correct. Seminoma is a germ-cell tumour of the testis. It is NOT an embryonic (blastoma) tumour, making it the exception here. Retinoblastoma, medulloblastoma and neuroblastoma are all embryonic tumours of immature precursor cells.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS embryonic). Neuroblastoma is an embryonic tumour of neural crest precursors.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: A benign tumour from all three germ cell layers is a teratoma
questions.question: What is a benign tumor called that is derived from all 3 germ cell layers?

explanations.A: Correct. A tumour derived from all three germ cell layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm) is a teratoma. The mature (well-differentiated) form is benign. Lymphoma, fibroma and myoma each arise from a single tissue type, not all three germ layers.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Lymphoma is a malignant tumour of lymphoid tissue, not a three-germ-layer tumour.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Fibroma is a benign tumour of fibrous connective tissue (single tissue type).
explanations.D: Incorrect. Myoma is a benign tumour of muscle (single tissue type).

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Haematoma is not a benign tumour
questions.question: Which is NOT a benign tumour:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS a benign tumour). Papilloma is a benign tumour of surface epithelium.
explanations.B: Correct. A haematoma is a localised collection of clotted blood, not a neoplasm. Despite its '-oma' suffix it is not a benign tumour. Papilloma, adenoma and fibroma, by contrast, are all true benign tumours.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS a benign tumour). Adenoma is a benign tumour of glandular epithelium.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS a benign tumour). Fibroma is a benign tumour of fibrous connective tissue.

questions.title: The mechanism of cyclosporine is inhibition of calcineurin
questions.question: The mechanism of action of cyclosporine is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cyclosporine does not act by non-specifically inhibiting white-cell division.
explanations.B: Correct. Cyclosporine binds cyclophilin, and the complex inhibits calcineurin. With calcineurin blocked, NFAT is not dephosphorylated and interleukin-2 transcription in T cells falls. It does not activate calcineurin, block interleukin receptors, or simply inhibit white-cell division.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cyclosporine does not block interleukin receptors; it blocks the intracellular calcineurin/NFAT pathway.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cyclosporine inhibits, rather than activates, calcineurin.

questions.title: Gum hyperplasia is a side effect of cyclosporine
questions.question: Which side effect is related to cyclosporine?

explanations.A: Correct. Gum (gingival) hyperplasia is a characteristic side effect of cyclosporine. It is one of the drug's recognisable, counsel-worthy adverse effects. Hypotension, muscular paralysis and arthritis are not typical cyclosporine effects.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cyclosporine tends to cause hypertension, not hypotension.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Muscular paralysis is not a recognised cyclosporine effect.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Arthritis is not a characteristic cyclosporine side effect.

questions.title: Cyclosporine toxicity does not include hypokalemia
questions.question: Toxic effects of cyclosporine DON'T include:

explanations.A: Incorrect (it IS a toxicity). Cyclosporine can cause hyperuricemia.
explanations.B: Correct. Cyclosporine tends to cause hyperkalemia, not hypokalemia. Hypokalemia is therefore the effect that is NOT among its toxicities. Hyperuricemia, nephrotoxicity and hypertension are all genuine cyclosporine toxicities.
explanations.C: Incorrect (it IS a toxicity). Nephrotoxicity is a major cyclosporine toxicity.
explanations.D: Incorrect (it IS a toxicity). Cyclosporine commonly causes hypertension.

questions.topic: Anticancer &Immunomodulator 2
questions.learning_objective: Recognise that cyclosporine toxicity does not include hypokalemia (it causes hyperkalemia, hyperuricemia, nephrotoxicity and hypertension).

questions.title: Cyclosporine is metabolized mainly by CYP3A4
questions.question: Cyclosporine is metabolized mainly by:

explanations.A: Incorrect. CYP2D6 is not the main enzyme metabolising cyclosporine.
explanations.B: Correct. Cyclosporine is metabolized mainly by hepatic CYP3A4. This underlies its many clinically important drug interactions, since CYP3A4 inhibitors raise and inducers lower its level. CYP2D6, CYP2C9 and CYP2C19 are not its principal metabolising enzymes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. CYP2C9 is not the principal cyclosporine-metabolising enzyme.
explanations.D: Incorrect. CYP2C19 is not the principal cyclosporine-metabolising enzyme.

questions.title: Cyclosporine is the drug of choice for prevention of post-transplant rejection
questions.question: The drug of choice for prevention of post-transplant rejection is:

explanations.A: Correct. Cyclosporine, a calcineurin inhibitor, is the drug of choice for prevention of post-transplant rejection. It suppresses the cell-mediated response that drives allograft rejection. Glucocorticoids are adjuncts, while alacizumab and anti-D immunoglobulin are not standard rejection-prophylaxis agents.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Glucocorticoids are used as adjuncts in immunosuppression, not as the first-choice agent for rejection prophylaxis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Alacizumab is not the standard agent for preventing transplant rejection.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Anti-D immunoglobulin is used to prevent Rh sensitisation, not transplant rejection.
